segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: and in doing so contradicts Luke who has Jesus saying a spirit does not have flesh and bones as you see I have.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: But here again he has failed to grasp the linguistics of the passage.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: Greek exegete d a Carson notes that the term flesh and blood was a common Jewish expression referring to man as a mortal being.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: A Bible work search reveals that the term appears five times in the New Testament and twice in intertestamental writings,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: all with the meaning of being mortal.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: Thus Paul is not at all contradicting luke; and once again,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: there is nothing here hinting at an exchange.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: Finally, Richard says that in um verses fifty one and fifty two, Paul uses the term um allagosamatha,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: which does not mean change in the sense of changing one thing into another thing, I'm quoting him, but is instead the verb of mercantile exchange, of trading one thing for another. Folks, this is a half truth and the wrong half.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: All anyone has to do is go to the major Greek lexicons, such as Liddell-Scott,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: BDAG, and Kittel's Theological Dictionary of the New Testament,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: and you'll discover, contrary to Richard's claim,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: that the primary meaning of the term is to change, to alter.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: The mercantile definition of trading one thing for another is a secondary definition.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: In fact, BDAG and TDNT list 1 Corinthians 15 under the primary definition of altering.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: Ladell Scott is silent on the verse.

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: In conclusion,

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: we've seen that the evidence for Jesus'

segments.speaker: Mike Licona
segments.text: resurrection is very good.
